artifacts.summary: Verifies the errors.json absence and three-way schema drift empirically, enumerates all readers/writers, studies events-append.sh/events-schema.json as the pattern to mirror, and recommends one reconciled schema plus append/update script design and deploy-path wiring.

memory_candidates.content: In this codebase's core scripts, 'schema-validated' means hand-written bash checks (required-arg presence, case-statement enums, jq type/shape checks) kept manually in sync with a documented JSON Schema file -- not a runtime call into a JSON-Schema validator library. events-append.sh (the reference pattern for validated append scripts) never invokes ajv or python jsonschema against events-schema.json even though python3's jsonschema package is installed on the dev machine. New validated-append scripts should follow this same hand-written-check idiom rather than introducing a new validation dependency.

When a task's own file_scope/manifest already exist (e.g. an abandoned superseding task whose directory was never created), the abandoned task's full description survives in specs/state.json even after its directory is gone -- `jq '.active_projects[] | select(.project_number==N)' specs/state.json` recovers the complete original description text (including verified defect inventories) for tasks that never got past creation, which is the authoritative source when a successor task says 'read the superseded task's directory' but that directory does not exist.

core/manifest.json's provides.scripts array is a flat, alphabetically-sorted filename list needing an explicit new entry per script, but provides.context's 'schemas' entry copies the whole context/schemas/ directory as a unit -- a new *-schema.json file needs no manifest change, only a new *.sh script does. Also: the headless 'Load Core' sync path does not always re-run copy_scripts for already-loaded extensions, so a brand-new script can land in the source store but silently fail to reach an already-deployed repo's .claude/scripts/ without a manual full resync -- verify post-deploy presence, don't assume authoring in the source store is sufficient.
